Subject:       Response to Third Request for Additional Information Regarding Emergency
               License Amendment Request: One-Time-Use Amendment to Allow Alternative
               Fuel Handling Method for the Recovery of Fuel Assembly DD41



By letter dated September 30, 2026 (Reference 1), in accordance with Title 10 of the Code of
Federal Regulations (10 CFR) 50.90, Application for amendment of license, construction permit,
or early site permit and 10 CFR 50.91, Notice for public comment; State consultation, Palisades
Energy, LLC (Palisades Energy) requested U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC)
approval of a one-time emergency change to the Renewed Facility Operating License (RFOL)
for Palisades Nuclear Plant (PNP). The proposed License Amendment Request (LAR) would
revise UFSAR Sections 9.11 Fuel Handling and Storage Systems, and 14.19 Fuel Handling
Accident, to facilitate transport of fuel assembly DD41 from the reactor utilizing different plant
equipment and following a different travel path than is described in the Updated Final Safety
Analysis Report (UFSAR).

On October 1, 2026, the NRC and Palisades Energy conducted a conference call in which the
NRC staff verbally and visually requested information in the form of questions related to the
proposed LAR. On October 2, 2026, a follow-up conference call was conducted between the
NRC and Palisades Energy. The purpose of the call was to provide verbal responses to the
questions raised and to identify responses required to be docketed . Palisades Energy provided
the responses to the request for additional information (RAI) in a letter dated October 2, 2026
(Reference 2).

By electronic mail (email) received on October 7, 2026, the NRC provided a second RAI
regarding the LAR. Palisades Energy provided the responses to the second request for
additional information (RAI) in a letter dated October 8, 2026 (Reference 3).

By email received on October 9, 2026, the NRC provided a third RAI regarding the LAR.

This letter contains no new regulatory commitments and no revisions to existing regulatory

                             Response to Request for Information

Background:

By letter dated September 30, 2026 (Reference 1 of cover letter), in accordance with Title 10 of
the Code of Federal Regulations (10 CFR) 50.90, Application for amendment of license,
construction permit, or early site permit and 10 CFR 50.91, Notice for public comment; State
consultation, Palisades Energy, LLC (Pal isades Energy) requested U.S. Nuclear Regulatory
Commission (NRC) approval of a one-time emergency change to the Renewed Facility
Operating License (RFOL) for Palisades Nuclear Plant (PNP). The proposed License
Amendment Request (LAR) would revise UFSAR Sections 9.11 Fuel Handling and Storage
Systems, and 14.19 Fuel Handling Accident, to facilitate transport of fuel assembly D041
(0D41) from the reactor utilizing different plant equipment and following a different travel path
than is described in the Updated Final Safety Analysis Report (UFSAR).

On October 1, 2026, the NRC and Palisades Energy conducted a conference call in which the
NRC staff verbally and visually requested information in the form of questions related to the
proposed LAR. On October 2, 2026, a follow-up conference call was conducted between the
NRC and Palisades Energy. The purpose of the call was to provide verbal responses to the
questions raised and to identify responses required to be docketed . Palisades Energy provided
the responses to the request for additional information (RAI) in a letter dated October 2, 2026
(Reference 2 of cover letter).

By electronic mail (email) received on October 7, 2026, the NRC provided a second RAI
regarding the LAR. Palisades Energy provided the responses to the second request for
additional information (RAI) in a letter dated October 8, 2026 (Reference 3 of cover letter).

By email received on October 9, 2026, the NRC provided a third RAI regarding the LAR. Each
RAI is presented below in bold type and is followed by the Palisades Energy response.

RAl-1a

In response to RAI 3 in the October 8, 2026, supplement, it was stated that "Once DD41 is
placed on the FTC pedestals, the extent of plastic deformation and overall assembly
alignment will be confirmed using cameras before lowering the canister lid." Please
describe the specific acceptance criteria that will be applied to determine whether the
observed residual bowing and deformation are acceptable prior to lid installation. In
addition, provide the supporting technical basis, including any engineering analyses,
calculations, or vendor evaluations, demonstrating that assemblies meeting these
acceptance criteria will not experience fuel rod damage during the subsequent lid-
lowering and recovery activities.

Response to RAl-1 a:

The specific acceptance criteria for lowering the Fuel Transfer Canister (FTC) lid , as specified in
FHSO-19A, Recovery of FA 0041 [Reference 1], consists of two parts. First, D041 will be
visually confirmed to be within the bounds of the FTC alignment tool to ensure that it does not
 PNP 2026-057
Page 3 of 6


sit misaligned on the horizontal plane. After positioning is confirmed , the alignment tool will then
be removed before the FTC lid is lowered.

The second acceptance criterion will be that no gap between DO41 and a pedestal shall be
greater than 2 inches. Using an underwater camera, OD41 seating on the FTC pedestals will be
verified from a horizontal view using markings on the alignment tool that represent 2 inches from
the pedestals. Based on an evaluation by the site's fuel vendor, FS1-0088338-1.0, Estimated
impact of cannister lid contacting 0041 based on assembly distortion [Reference 2], the
predicted plastic deformation should not exceed 3 inches from the horizontal and the largest
gaps between OD41 and the pedestals are expected to exist at the top end of the assembly. If
any gaps are determined to be greater than 2 inches, work will stop and the site will re-evaluate .

RAl-1b:

In addition, the response to RAI 3 states "Based on a review by our fuel vendor, the
assembly is expected to straighten out without risk of fuel cladding failure inside the
FTC" and "As long as the fuel rods remain within the envelope defined by the inner
surface of the FTC lid, there is no potential for fuel rod failure during lowering of the lid."
Given that the full extent of assembly damage may not be completely characterized, on
what basis can it be concluded that there is "no potential" for fuel rod failure during
installation of the FTC lid? Please describe the analytical, empirical, or vendor-supported
justification underlying these two statements.

Response to RAl-1 b:

Visual evaluations have not identified any of the fuel rods to have experienced damage from
DO41 tilting onto the core shroud , with the impacts absorbed by the non-fuel hardware (upper
tie plate, guide bars, and spacer grids). To confirm no fuel rod cladding failure, numerous water
chemistry samples have been taken to detect fission product leakage. During lowering of the
FTC lid, per FS1-0088338-1 .0, [Reference 2] , it is expected that the non-fuel hardware will
absorb any undesired forces and strain externally placed on the assembly.

RAl-2a:

Provide information, including supporting calculations, characterizing the potential
radiological conditions during removal of the cask from the reactor cavity water, to which
workers in containment and the fuel handling building may be exposed assuming a
fraction of the fuel rods fail when the fuel transfer cask lid is lowered onto the assembly.
The response should specifically address the expected airborne contamination
conditions associated with this scenario.

Response to RAl-2a:

While the FTC lid is being lowered, there will be a minimum of 20 feet of water between DO41
and the water surface. Using staff guidance from Regulatory Guide 1.183 Revision 0, Appendix
B, Assumptions for Evaluating the Radiological Consequences of a Fuel Handling Accident, to
consider the decontamination effects of water from a fuel accident release, workers would be
exposed only to the noble gases within DO41. According to the isotopic analysis of OD41, the
only remaining noble gas radioisotope is Krypton-85 (Kr-85), which is limited to an activity of
3,734 Curies (Ci) for the entire assembly.
 PNP 2026-057
Page 4 of 6



To bound all postulated scenarios during lowering of the FTC lid, the following evaluation
assumes a worst-case accident of all 216 fuel rods undergoing complete loss of cladding
integrity. In accordance with Regulatory Position 3.2 (Table 3) of Regulatory Guide 1.183, the
fractional release of Kr-85 from the gap between the cladding and fuel pellet is assumed to be
10%. Applying the Table 3 release fraction results in a total gaseous activity of 373.4 Ci in
containment.

Since this postulated scenario is to quantify immediate local worker dose, assuming a dispersal
into the entire containment volume would not be realistic. Therefore, the following dose
approximation assumes all activity has been instantaneously dispersed into a local
compartment of 20 x 20 x 20 feet where a worker is standing for five minutes (300 seconds).
The five-minute duration is based on the conservative assumption that the worker must place
work in a safe condition before evacuating the containment building. Since Kr-85 radiological
effects are known only to be detrimental by means of external submersion, absorption by means
of inhalation is not considered .

RAl-2b:

Describe what immediate actions are planned if there are unexpected airborne monitor
alarms when the FTC is removed from the reactor cavity water.

Response to RAl-2b:

The activity-specific ALARA plan and Radiation Work Permit establish radiological controls
through the station's existing Radiation Protection (RP) programs and approved procedures.
These controls include radiation and airborne-radioactivity monitoring, contamination controls,
personnel dosimetry, respiratory protection, restricted access, RP coverage, and radiological
hold points. Required radiological surveys and Chemistry sampling evaluations support
authorization to proceed with designated phases, including removal of the canister from the
water.
Portable continuous air monitors may alarm during the lift phase as the FTC is moved from
below the water surface to above the water surface. RP personnel will monitor detector
response throughout canister operations and evaluate alarm conditions based on detector
behavior. A rapid increase in detector response is expected during the lift due to changing
geometry and increasing background dose rates as shielding effects are reduced. In contrast, a
sustained gradual increase in detector response that is inconsistent with expected lifting
activities may be indicative of airborne radioactivity and would prompt further evaluation by RP
personnel. RP will provide continuous oversight of canister operations and direct appropriate
actions in accordance with station procedures.
An unexpected portable continuous air monitor alarm would require the work to stop and
notification of Operations and RP Management. RP would implement personnel protective
actions, including withdrawal or evacuation as required by applicable procedures, while
Operations would direct any actions necessary to place 0D41 and FTC in a safe condition. RP
would evaluate radiological conditions and the adequacy of controls, with Chemistry and
Engineering support as appropriate.
Further planned work would remain suspended until the condition is evaluated, necessary
changes to controls are implemented, and required authorizations are obtained in accordance
with station procedures. Affected personnel are briefed before work resumes.


RAl-3

Describe the FTC design features related to water and air infill, as well as drainage, as
these functions are important to ensuring that the 133-hour limit on FTC out-of-pool time
adequately protects fuel rod oxidation limits and maintains cladding integrity.
Specifically, when the FTC lid is installed while the FTC remains underwater, is there any
potential for air to become entrapped within the canister such that portions of the fuel
rods may not remain fully submerged? If air entrapment is possible, describe any design
 PNP 2026-057
Page 6 of 6


features or operational mechanisms used to remove trapped air and ensure complete
water coverage.

Further, if there is any condition under which trapped air could expose fuel rods to air
once the lid is placed, clarify whether the 133-hour out-of-water time limit would initiate
at that point. Provide technical and procedural basis supporting the response.

Response to RAl-3:

The FTC cover, with the end-mounted shield gate, is designed to be self-venting in both the
horizontal and vertical orientation . The shield gate is nominally 9-inches thick and the gate guide
plates provide a 9-1/4-inch channel for the gate to slide in. Thus, there is a nominal 1/4-inch gap
between the gate and the guide plates that will allow venting via the gate gap. The gate is also
provided with a machined groove on the lower portion of the gate (while in the horizontal
position) to facilitate drainage of the water contained within the canister when it is raised out of
the reactor cavity water to minimize the time spent waiting for water drainage to complete. In the
horizontal alignment, the top of the shield gate extends above the top of the fuel assembly
cavity, thus the air in the fuel assembly cavity will be vented via the gate-to-gate guide plate gap
when the FTC cover is first submerged. After the FTC cover is submerged, per FHSO-19A,
[Reference 1], a submersible camera will be used to visually determine the effectiveness of the
fuel assembly void venting. If the venting is determined to be insufficient, further action will be
taken to complete the venting process as needed.

When the FTC is upended for vertical placement in the Spent Fuel Pool, the machined groove in
the gate will ensure the entire fuel assembly is completely and promptly vented as the FTC is
lowered under the water. Based on these features , there is no plausible scenario in which
trapped air could expose the fuel rods once the FTC lid is placed.

The 133-hour limit per HOLTEC Report Hl-2261312 Rev. 0, Thermal Evaluation of Fuel
Transfer Operations using Fuel Transfer Canister at Palisades NPP [Reference 3), is built on
the assumption that all water has been drained from the FTC by gravity. FHSO-19A, [Reference
1] will start the 133-hour clock when the FTC is removed from the reactor cavity water and stop
it when the FTC is fully submerged in the Spent Fuel Pool.
